business_problem: Mountain Warehouse needed offline-first store apps that could keep stock, pricing, and parcel workflows synchronized despite patchy in-store connectivity.
solution_summary: Mountain Warehouse uses MongoDB Atlas as the data backbone for a growing suite of retail store apps built to work even when shop-floor Wi-Fi is unreliable. Product, stock, pricing, returns, and click-and-collect data is pushed from the company's SQL data warehouse into Atlas, then synchronized to Android and React Native applications through Atlas Device Sync and App Services so changes appear as soon as a device reconnects. The same platform supports Product Checker, Stock Count, and parcel-scanning workflows, while partitioning ensures staff only receive the right regional product and currency data. This architecture replaced manual store tasks with app-assisted workflows and helped the retailer scale to 25 MongoDB-backed microservices and applications.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Stores product, stock, pricing, and parcel data for store-assistant applications.

solution_components.name: Atlas Device Sync
solution_components.role: Synchronizes offline-first mobile app data back to Atlas when devices reconnect.

solution_components.name: App Services
solution_components.role: Enables partition-based sync configuration for store and regional data.
